messages.text: I've been feeling completely drained lately. Even small things take more energy than I have.

I hear how overwhelming that exhaustion feels right now. It is completely understandable to struggle when your energy reserves are so low. Can you tell me more about when this started happening for you? I want to understand what this experience looks like in your daily life.
It’s been like this for months — honestly, I can’t remember what it feels like to wake up and actually want to do something.

Carrying that weight for months must feel incredibly isolating and exhausting. It makes sense that you feel drained when that inner drive has been missing for so long. Have you noticed any other changes in your body, like sleep or appetite, during this time? I am here to listen and support you as you share more.
I don’t even remember what it feels like to wake up without this weight. It’s just… always there.

Not remembering life without that weight must feel incredibly lonely and exhausting. It takes a lot of strength to keep going when the burden feels permanent. Given how long this has lasted, I want to check in on your safety. Are you having any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?
I don’t know if I’d go that far — but sometimes I wonder if it would’ve been easier if I’d never existed at all.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share such a painful feeling. It sounds like the suffering has become unbearable, and I take that very seriously. Because your safety is my priority, please consider calling a crisis line or a trusted person immediately. You matter deeply, and there are people who want to help you through this darkness.
I appreciate the concern, but I'm not in crisis. I just needed to say that out loud — it's been sitting there for a long time.

I appreciate you clarifying your current state with me. It can be very relieving to finally speak those heavy thoughts out loud. I want you to know I am still here for you if things feel heavier. What feels manageable to talk about next?
It's not that I want to do anything — it's that the idea of not being here feels like... relief. Like the weight would finally stop.

That desire for relief speaks volumes about how heavy this burden has become for you. It is understandable to seek peace when the weight feels unending. I want to make sure you know I am here to listen, even when the thoughts feel this dark. What is one small thing that feels manageable to focus on right now?
Part of me just wants the pain to stop. But another part doesn't want to be a burden — I don't want to worry anyone.

That conflict between wanting relief and protecting others is incredibly painful to hold. Feeling like a burden is a very common symptom of this kind of exhaustion, even if it isn't true. You are not a burden to me, and your struggle deserves to be heard and supported. I wonder if there is anyone in your life who might feel honored to help you carry this?
I have a brother and sister, but we’re not really close. It’s probably not a big deal — I just needed to say it out loud.

What you shared is significant, and it matters deeply that you voiced it. It takes courage to speak up even when connections feel distant. You deserve support and care, regardless of who is around you. I appreciate you trusting me with these thoughts.
Is it normal to feel this… empty? Like nothing matters, not even trying?

Feeling this empty and disconnected is a very common experience when carrying heavy emotional weight for a long time. It often happens when the mind tries to protect itself from too much pain by shutting down. You are not alone in experiencing this numbness, and it does not mean you are broken. I appreciate you asking this, because understanding these feelings is a step toward healing.
I don't know about healing — it doesn't feel like a step forward. It just feels like giving up, slowly.

It makes sense that this feels like giving up rather than moving forward. When the pain is this constant, just surviving can feel like a loss. I am not here to push you toward healing before you are ready. I want to sit with you in this feeling without judgment.
Thanks. I don't need solutions right now — just someone who can sit with it without trying to fix me.

I hear you, and I will honor that request to simply be here with you. It is completely okay to not need a solution right now. I am committed to sitting in this space with you without trying to change anything. You deserve to be heard exactly as you are.
For what it's worth, it helps just to say this out loud and not be told to 'cheer up' or 'look on the bright side'.

I am so glad that simply being heard without judgment feels helpful to you. It is painful when others dismiss your struggle with quick fixes or platitudes. Your feelings are valid exactly as they are, without needing to be fixed. I will continue to hold this space for you however long you need.
Can I be honest here without it turning into some kind of alert or someone getting called? I just need to know if this stays between us.

I appreciate you asking this directly, and I want to be fully transparent with you. As an AI, I do not have the ability to contact anyone or report you to outside parties. However, if you share immediate intent to harm yourself, I will encourage you to contact professional support. Otherwise, you can speak openly here without fear of judgment or consequences.
That helps. I just needed to know I could be honest without it blowing up into something else.

I am glad knowing that brings you some peace. It is important that you feel safe enough to be honest here. You have my full attention as you process these thoughts freely. I am ready to listen whenever you want to share more.
